# Model and source

* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Yusuff_2026_voriconazole"))$reference`
* Description: `r rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Yusuff_2026_voriconazole"))$description`
* Article (open access): <https://doi.org/10.1128/aac.00098-26>

Yusuff 2026 describes intravenous voriconazole in adults on extracorporeal
membrane oxygenation (ECMO) with a one-compartment model whose total clearance
changes with time since the first dose. Two parallel pathways add up:

* an **intrinsic clearance** that rises logistically from an early level
  `CL1` = 6.22 L/h to a late level `CL2` = 22.26 L/h, with midpoint
  `Tswitch` = 88 h and a slope fixed at 0.1 1/h (equation 1), and
* an **apparent sequestration clearance** into the ECMO circuit that starts at
  `CLseq0` = 17.68 L/h and decays with a half-life of 4.17 h (equation 2).

CYP2C19 intermediate and poor metabolizers (IM/PM) have a 36% lower late
clearance (`exp(-0.44)` = 0.644). The volume (144.79 L) scales linearly with
body weight relative to 70 kg, as written in the authors' Monolix code in the
supplement.

# Population

Thirty-one adults on ECMO at University Hospitals Leicester (UK) contributed
131 plasma samples between August 2021 and May 2025 (Yusuff 2026 Results,
Table 1). Mean age was 39.9 years (range 19-58), mean weight 86.8 kg (range
49-134), and 54.8% were female. Most patients were on venovenous ECMO
(93.5%), mainly for influenza (64.5%) or COVID-19 (19.4%) pneumonitis.
Corticosteroids were given to 87.2% and a proton pump inhibitor to all
patients. CYP2C19 phenotypes were 12 normal, 12 intermediate, 5 rapid, 1 poor
and 1 ultrarapid metabolizer, so 13 of 31 (42%) were in the IM/PM group that
carries the genotype effect.

The same information is available programmatically via
`readModelDb("Yusuff_2026_voriconazole")$population`.

# Source trace

| Element | Value | Source |
|---|---|---|
| One-compartment structure, `pkmodel(V, Cl)` | -- | Supplement, Monolix model code |
| Intrinsic clearance, logistic in time | `CL1 + (CL2 - CL1) / (1 + exp(-k (t - Tswitch)))` | Equation 1; supplement code |
| Logistic slope `k` | 0.1 1/h (fixed) | Results text below equation 3; supplement code |
| Sequestration clearance | `CLseq0 * exp(-ln(2) / T1/2,seq * t)` | Equation 2; supplement code |
| Total clearance | `CLintr + CLseq` | Equation 3; supplement code |
| Weight scaling of V | `V * (WT / 70)` | Supplement code only |
| `lvc` | V = 144.79 L | Table 2 |
| `lcl` | CL1 = 6.22 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lcl_late` | CL2 = 22.26 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lcl_t50` | Tswitch = 87.96 h | Table 2 |
| `lcl_exp_component` | CLseq0 = 17.68 L/h | Table 2 |
| `lcl_exp_kdes` | log(2) / 4.17 h | Table 2 (T1/2,seq = 4.17 h) |
| `e_cyp2c19impm_cl_late` | -0.44 (log scale) | Table 2; Results text ('36% lower CL2') |
| `etalvc` | 27.6% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalcl` | 77.0% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalcl_late` | 86.7% CV | Table 2 |
| `etalcl_t50` | 81.9% CV | Table 2 |
| `addSd` | 0.091 mg/L | Table 2 |
| `propSd` | 0.12 | Table 2 |

IIV variances are `log(1 + CV^2)`, inverting the Table 2 footnote
`CV = sqrt(exp(omega^2) - 1)`.

```{r model}
mod <- rxode2::rxode2(readModelDb("Yusuff_2026_voriconazole"))
eta_names <- c("etalvc", "etalcl", "etalcl_late", "etalcl_t50")

# Solve with the random effects supplied in `params`. rxode2 then draws no
# etas and warns that the simulation runs "without 'omega'"; that warning is
# expected here and is the only one muffled.
solve_fixed_eta <- function(...) {
  withCallingHandlers(
    rxSolve(...),
    warning = function(w) {
      if (grepl("without 'omega'", conditionMessage(w), fixed = TRUE)) {
        invokeRestart("muffleWarning")
      }
    }
  )
}
```

# Clearance over time

The typical-value clearance trajectory reproduces the Results text: at the
first dose the sequestration pathway roughly quadruples the early intrinsic
clearance, it is gone within a day, and the intrinsic clearance then rises to
22.3 L/h in normal metabolizers (14.3 L/h in IM/PM) over 3-5 days.

```{r cl-trajectory}
grid <- c(0, seq(0.5, 240, by = 0.5))
cl_events <- bind_rows(
  tibble(id = 1L, CYP2C19_IM = 0L),
  tibble(id = 2L, CYP2C19_IM = 1L)
) |>
  tidyr::crossing(time = grid) |>
  mutate(evid = 0L, amt = 0, cmt = "central", WT = 70, CYP2C19_PM = 0L) |>
  arrange(id, time)
# Typical values: every eta set to zero for both subjects.
eta_zero <- data.frame(id = 1:2, matrix(0, 2, 4, dimnames = list(NULL, eta_names)))
cl_sim <- as.data.frame(solve_fixed_eta(mod, cl_events, params = eta_zero, keep = "CYP2C19_IM")) |>
  mutate(genotype = ifelse(CYP2C19_IM == 1, "IM/PM", "NM/RM/UM"))

# Same-parameter closed form: the model's cl must equal equations 1-3 exactly.
cl_formula <- function(t, impm) {
  cl2 <- 22.26 * exp(-0.44 * impm)
  6.22 + (cl2 - 6.22) / (1 + exp(-0.1 * (t - 87.96))) +
    17.68 * exp(-log(2) / 4.17 * t)
}
stopifnot(
  max(abs(cl_sim$cl - cl_formula(cl_sim$time, cl_sim$CYP2C19_IM))) < 1e-8
)

cl_sim |>
  filter(time %in% c(0, 12, 24, 48, 88, 168, 240)) |>
  select(genotype, time, cl_intr, cl_seq, cl) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Genotype" = genotype, "Time (h)" = time, "CL intrinsic (L/h)" = cl_intr,
    "CL sequestration (L/h)" = cl_seq, "CL total (L/h)" = cl
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Typical-value clearance components over time (WT = 70 kg).")
```

```{r cl-plot, fig.cap = "Typical-value total clearance over time by CYP2C19 group (equations 1-3 of Yusuff 2026)."}
ggplot(cl_sim, aes(time, cl, colour = genotype)) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time since first dose (h)", y = "Total clearance (L/h)", colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw()
```

# Virtual cohort

Doses are weight-based, so the cohort needs a weight distribution. Yusuff 2026
reports mean 86.8 kg and range 49-134 kg but no SD; weights are drawn from a
normal distribution with mean 86.8 kg and SD 20 kg truncated to the observed
range. Because both the dose and the volume scale with weight, concentrations
are only weakly sensitive to this choice (clearance is not weight-scaled).

```{r cohort}
# rxSetSeed() seeds rxode2's own draws (IIV); set.seed() seeds the R draws
# of weight and genotype below.
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20261113)
set.seed(20261113)
n_per_group <- 200
draw_wt <- function(n) {
  w <- rnorm(4 * n, 86.8, 20)
  w <- w[w >= 49 & w <= 134]
  w[seq_len(n)]
}

# Interindividual random effects drawn once per virtual patient, so that the
# same patients can be given every regimen (the omega matrix is diagonal).
omega_sd <- sqrt(diag(mod$omega))[eta_names]
draw_eta <- function(ids) {
  eta <- vapply(omega_sd, function(sd) rnorm(length(ids), 0, sd), numeric(length(ids)))
  data.frame(id = ids, eta)
}

# Doses (mg/kg) at 0, 12, 24, ... h; the regimen switches at dose 11 (120 h)
# for regimens 2 and 3 (two loading doses + eight maintenance doses).
regimen_mgkg <- function(regimen, n_doses = 21) {
  dose_no <- seq_len(n_doses)
  switch(regimen,
    "Regimen 1" = ifelse(dose_no <= 2, 6, 4),
    "Regimen 2" = ifelse(dose_no <= 2, 6, ifelse(dose_no <= 10, 4, 6)),
    "Regimen 3" = ifelse(dose_no <= 2, 8, ifelse(dose_no <= 10, 6, 8))
  )
}

make_events <- function(subjects, regimen, obs_times) {
  mgkg <- regimen_mgkg(regimen)
  dose_times <- (seq_along(mgkg) - 1) * 12
  doses <- subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(dose_no = seq_along(mgkg)) |>
    mutate(
      time = dose_times[dose_no], amt = mgkg[dose_no] * WT,
      rate = amt / 2, evid = 1L, cmt = "central"
    ) |>
    select(-dose_no)
  obs <- subjects |>
    tidyr::crossing(time = obs_times) |>
    mutate(amt = 0, rate = 0, evid = 0L, cmt = "central")
  bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
    mutate(regimen = regimen) |>
    arrange(id, time, desc(evid))
}
```

Infusions run over 2 h, the upper end of the 1.5-2 h used in the study.

# Replication of Figure 2

Figure 2 of Yusuff 2026 shows the median and 90% prediction interval of
concentrations under standard dosing (6 mg/kg q12h x 2, then 4 mg/kg q12h),
split into normal/rapid/ultrarapid ("wild-type") and IM/PM patients.

```{r fig2-sim}
subjects_fig2 <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(2 * n_per_group),
  WT = draw_wt(2 * n_per_group),
  CYP2C19_IM = rep(c(0L, 1L), each = n_per_group),
  CYP2C19_PM = 0L
)
ev_fig2 <- make_events(subjects_fig2, "Regimen 1", seq(0, 240, by = 0.5))
sim_fig2 <- as.data.frame(rxSolve(mod, ev_fig2, keep = c("CYP2C19_IM", "WT"))) |>
  mutate(genotype = ifelse(CYP2C19_IM == 1, "IM/PM", "Wild-type (NM/RM/UM)"))
```

```{r fig2-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 2 of Yusuff 2026: median and 90% prediction interval of voriconazole concentrations under standard dosing, by CYP2C19 group (200 virtual patients per group). Dashed lines mark the 2-5.5 mg/L therapeutic range."}
fig2_summ <- sim_fig2 |>
  group_by(genotype, time) |>
  summarise(
    p05 = quantile(Cc, 0.05), p50 = median(Cc), p95 = quantile(Cc, 0.95),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
ggplot(fig2_summ, aes(time, p50, colour = genotype, fill = genotype)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = p05, ymax = p95), alpha = 0.25, colour = NA) +
  geom_line(linewidth = 1) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(2, 5.5), linetype = "dashed", colour = "red") +
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0, 240, 24)) +
  labs(x = "Time (hours)", y = "Voriconazole concentration (mg/L)", colour = NULL, fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The simulated medians follow the published ones: a first peak near 2.5 mg/L,
the highest troughs around 36-48 h, then a decline as intrinsic clearance
rises, with the wild-type median trough falling below 2 mg/L by about day 4
while the IM/PM median stays higher. Read off the published figure, the late
IM/PM median trough is about 1.1-1.5 mg/L, somewhat below the simulated
value (about 1.9 mg/L); the wild-type median and both 90% intervals agree
closely.

# Replication of Figure 3 (probability of target attainment)

Figure 3 of Yusuff 2026 classifies simulated concentrations at 48, 168 and
240 h as sub-therapeutic (< 2 mg/L), on-target (2-5.5 mg/L) or
supra-therapeutic (> 5.5 mg/L) for three regimens. The virtual patients here
mix the genotype groups in the study proportion (13 of 31 IM/PM), and the
same 200 patients (same weights, genotypes and random effects) receive each
regimen, so regimens 1 and 2 are identical until the switch at 120 h. The
classification uses the individual predictions `Cc`, without residual error.

```{r fig3-sim}
subjects_pta <- tibble(
  id = seq_len(n_per_group),
  WT = draw_wt(n_per_group),
  CYP2C19_IM = as.integer(runif(n_per_group) < 13 / 31),
  CYP2C19_PM = 0L
)
eta_pta <- draw_eta(subjects_pta$id)
pta_times <- c(48, 168, 240)
sim_pta <- lapply(c("Regimen 1", "Regimen 2", "Regimen 3"), function(r) {
  ev <- make_events(subjects_pta, r, pta_times)
  as.data.frame(solve_fixed_eta(mod, ev, params = eta_pta, keep = "regimen"))
}) |>
  bind_rows()

pta <- sim_pta |>
  mutate(category = cut(Cc, c(-Inf, 2, 5.5, Inf),
    labels = c("Sub-therapeutic", "On-target", "Supra-therapeutic"),
    right = FALSE
  )) |>
  count(regimen, time, category, .drop = FALSE) |>
  group_by(regimen, time) |>
  mutate(pct = 100 * n / sum(n)) |>
  ungroup()

published_pta <- tribble(
  ~regimen, ~time, ~category, ~published,
  "Regimen 1", 48, "Sub-therapeutic", 43.9,
  "Regimen 1", 48, "On-target", 47.6,
  "Regimen 1", 48, "Supra-therapeutic", 8.5,
  "Regimen 1", 168, "Sub-therapeutic", 75.8,
  "Regimen 1", 168, "On-target", 19.0,
  "Regimen 1", 168, "Supra-therapeutic", 5.2,
  "Regimen 1", 240, "Sub-therapeutic", 82.9,
  "Regimen 1", 240, "On-target", 13.7,
  "Regimen 1", 240, "Supra-therapeutic", 100 - 82.9 - 13.7,
  "Regimen 2", 48, "Sub-therapeutic", 43.9,
  "Regimen 2", 48, "On-target", 47.6,
  "Regimen 2", 48, "Supra-therapeutic", 8.5,
  "Regimen 2", 168, "Sub-therapeutic", 64.1,
  "Regimen 2", 168, "On-target", 26.3,
  "Regimen 2", 168, "Supra-therapeutic", 9.6,
  "Regimen 2", 240, "Sub-therapeutic", 71.0,
  "Regimen 2", 240, "On-target", 22.0,
  "Regimen 2", 240, "Supra-therapeutic", 7.0,
  "Regimen 3", 48, "Sub-therapeutic", 30.0,
  "Regimen 3", 48, "On-target", 48.4,
  "Regimen 3", 48, "Supra-therapeutic", 21.6,
  "Regimen 3", 168, "Sub-therapeutic", 57.1,
  "Regimen 3", 168, "On-target", 27.7,
  "Regimen 3", 168, "Supra-therapeutic", 15.2,
  "Regimen 3", 240, "Sub-therapeutic", 63.9,
  "Regimen 3", 240, "On-target", 24.7,
  "Regimen 3", 240, "Supra-therapeutic", 11.4
)

pta_cmp <- pta |>
  mutate(category = as.character(category)) |>
  inner_join(published_pta, by = c("regimen", "time", "category")) |>
  mutate(diff = pct - published)
stopifnot(nrow(pta_cmp) == 27L)

pta_cmp |>
  select(regimen, time, category, pct, published, diff) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Regimen" = regimen, "Time (h)" = time, "Category" = category,
    "Simulated (%)" = pct, "Yusuff 2026 Fig. 3 (%)" = published,
    "Difference (points)" = diff
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 1, caption = "Target attainment: simulation (200 virtual patients per regimen) vs Figure 3 of Yusuff 2026 (1,000 virtual patients). The 240 h supra-therapeutic value for regimen 1 is unlabelled in the figure and is taken as the remainder.")
```

The simulation puts about 10 percentage points fewer patients in
the sub-therapeutic band than Figure 3 does, in every regimen and at every
time, while the ordering across times and regimens is the same. Classifying
the simulated observations with residual error instead of `Cc` does not close
the gap. Possible causes are the weight distribution, the genotype mix and the
infusion duration used in the published simulations, none of which is
reported; no parameter has been adjusted to close it.

```{r fig3-plot, fig.cap = "Replicates Figure 3 of Yusuff 2026: proportion of virtual patients below, within and above the 2-5.5 mg/L range at 48, 168 and 240 h."}
ggplot(pta, aes(factor(time), pct, fill = category)) +
  geom_col() +
  facet_wrap(~regimen) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("Sub-therapeutic" = "#3B75AF", "On-target" = "#519E3E", "Supra-therapeutic" = "#C53A32")) +
  labs(x = "Timepoint (h)", y = "Proportion of patients (%)", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

```{r fig3-check}
# Same patients, same doses until 120 h: regimens 1 and 2 must give identical
# concentrations at 48 h (residual error excluded).
c48 <- function(r) sim_pta$Cc[sim_pta$regimen == r & sim_pta$time == 48]
stopifnot(isTRUE(all.equal(c48("Regimen 1"), c48("Regimen 2"))))

# Centre-of-distribution checks. The simulation sits about 10 points from
# Figure 3 in the sub-therapeutic band (see text); a mis-transcribed clearance
# or volume moves these proportions by far more than that.
stopifnot(
  median(abs(pta_cmp$diff)) < 15,
  # The paper's headline: attainment worsens from 48 h to 240 h under
  # standard dosing, and the escalated regimens lessen but do not prevent it.
  with(pta_cmp, pct[regimen == "Regimen 1" & time == 240 & category == "Sub-therapeutic"] >
    pct[regimen == "Regimen 1" & time == 48 & category == "Sub-therapeutic"] + 20)
)
```

# PKNCA validation

Yusuff 2026 reports no non-compartmental parameters, so there is no published
NCA table to compare against. The NCA below summarises exposure in the first
dosing interval (0-12 h) and in a late interval (216-228 h) for the standard
regimen, by CYP2C19 group. By 216 h the intrinsic clearance has
reached its late level, so the ratio of the IM/PM to the wild-type median AUC
over that interval should be close to `1 / exp(-0.44)` = 1.55, the inverse of
the genotype effect on the late clearance.

```{r pknca}
conc_df <- sim_fig2 |>
  select(id, time, Cc, genotype) |>
  filter(!is.na(Cc))
dose_df <- ev_fig2 |>
  filter(evid == 1) |>
  left_join(distinct(sim_fig2, id, genotype), by = "id") |>
  select(id, time, amt, genotype)

conc_obj <- PKNCAconc(conc_df, Cc ~ time | genotype + id)
dose_obj <- PKNCAdose(dose_df, amt ~ time | genotype + id)
intervals <- data.frame(
  start = c(0, 216), end = c(12, 228),
  cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE, auclast = TRUE
)
nca_res <- pk.nca(PKNCAdata(conc_obj, dose_obj, intervals = intervals))

nca_summ <- as.data.frame(nca_res) |>
  filter(PPTESTCD %in% c("cmax", "cmin", "auclast")) |>
  group_by(genotype, start, end, PPTESTCD) |>
  summarise(median = median(PPORRES), .groups = "drop") |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = median)

# Late-phase exposure is higher in IM/PM, whose late clearance is 36% lower.
# Medians of 200 subjects per group; the ratio moves by far more than this
# window if the genotype effect is dropped or its sign is flipped.
late_auc_ratio <-
  nca_summ$auclast[nca_summ$start == 216 & nca_summ$genotype == "IM/PM"] /
    nca_summ$auclast[nca_summ$start == 216 & nca_summ$genotype == "Wild-type (NM/RM/UM)"]
stopifnot(late_auc_ratio > 1.2, late_auc_ratio < 2.2)
late_auc_ratio

nca_summ |>
  mutate(interval = paste0(start, "-", end, " h")) |>
  select(genotype, interval, cmax, cmin, auclast) |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "CYP2C19 group" = genotype, "Interval" = interval, "Cmax (mg/L)" = cmax,
    "Cmin (mg/L)" = cmin, "AUC0-12 (mg*h/L)" = auclast
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Median NCA by CYP2C19 group, standard dosing (6 mg/kg q12h x 2 then 4 mg/kg q12h).")
```

The first interval follows a 6 mg/kg dose and the late interval a 4 mg/kg
dose. In the wild-type group the late AUC is about the same as the first-dose
AUC despite the smaller dose and the accumulation of nine earlier doses, which
reflects the roughly fourfold rise in intrinsic clearance.

# Simulated troughs vs the observed troughs

The observed trough means in Yusuff 2026 Results were 3.1 mg/L (days 1-5),
2.5 mg/L (days 6-10) and 2.1 mg/L (days 11-14). These come from patients with
individualised doses and sampling and are a plausibility check only.

```{r troughs}
trough_df <- sim_fig2 |>
  filter(time %in% seq(12, 240, by = 12)) |>
  mutate(window = cut(time, c(0, 120, 240), labels = c("Days 1-5", "Days 6-10"))) |>
  group_by(window) |>
  summarise(sim_mean = mean(sim), sim_median = median(sim), .groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(observed_mean = c(3.1, 2.5))

trough_df |>
  dplyr::rename(
    "Window" = window, "Simulated mean trough (mg/L)" = sim_mean,
    "Simulated median trough (mg/L)" = sim_median,
    "Observed mean trough (mg/L)" = observed_mean
  ) |>
  knitr::kable(digits = 2, caption = "Simulated troughs (standard dosing, both genotype groups pooled 1:1) vs observed trough means.")
```

# Assumptions and deviations

* **Weight scaling of V.** The main text and Table 2 do not mention body
  weight, but the authors' Monolix code in the supplement scales the volume as
  `V * (WT/70)`. The packaged model follows the code, so Table 2's V of
  144.79 L applies to a 70 kg patient.
* **Time origin.** `t` in equations 1-2 is time since the first voriconazole
  dose. Most patients (25/31) started voriconazole within 24 h of ECMO
  cannulation; the model has no separate ECMO-start time.
* **Logistic slope.** `k` = 0.1 1/h is a fixed constant written as a literal
  in the authors' code; it appears as the literal `0.1` in `model()` rather
  than as an `ini()` parameter.
* **Genotype covariate.** The single IM/PM effect is coded as
  `CYP2C19_IM + CYP2C19_PM` (mutually exclusive indicators). The reference
  group pools normal, rapid and ultrarapid metabolizers, matching the
  "wild-type" group of Figures 2 and S5. The paper classes `*2/*17` as IM.
* **Residual error.** Table 2 reports an additive SD and a proportional
  coefficient without naming the Monolix error model; the default Monolix
  `combined1` form (`a + b*f`) is used.
* **Dosing in simulations.** Infusions last 2 h (the study used 1.5-2 h).
  Doses use total body weight; the study used adjusted body weight for obese
  patients, but height is not reported, so this adjustment is not reproduced.
* **Weight distribution.** No SD is reported; a normal distribution with SD
  20 kg truncated to 49-134 kg is assumed.
* **Cohort size.** 200 virtual patients per group or regimen, compared with
  1,000 in the paper.
* **Target attainment.** The simulated sub-therapeutic fractions run about
  10 percentage points below Figure 3 throughout (see above); the cause is not
  identifiable from the published information.
* **Errata.** No erratum or correction was found in Europe PMC for this article (checked 2026-11-13).
